skill.name: supabase-automation
skill.description: Automate Supabase administration through Rube MCP, including schema inspection, SQL execution, storage, edge functions, and project health workflows.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to manage Supabase projects, inspect schemas, run SQL, and review services.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code spans around MCP tool names and parameters. Real risks remain: external Rube MCP use, Supabase API key retrieval, and arbitrary SQL mutations against live projects.

remediation.issue: Supabase API key retrieval can expose live project secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before using SUPABASE_GET_PROJECT_API_KEYS and always mask full key values in responses, logs, and saved files.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary SQL execution can mutate or delete production data.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only mode for SELECT queries, inspect schemas first, and require approval before INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL statements.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on an external MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Document what data may be shared with Rube MCP and ask users to approve the endpoint before connecting sensitive Supabase projects.

content.value_statement: Supabase administration often requires switching between dashboards, SQL tools, and API references. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Find Supabase projects, organizations, and project references through Rube MCP tools.
List tables, views, schemas, indexes, relationships, and generated TypeScript types.
Query tables with filters, sorting, pagination, and selected columns.
Run SQL through Supabase MCP tools, including read-only queries and mutation workflows.
Inspect edge functions, storage buckets, authentication configuration, and service health.
Document common Supabase parameter formats, pagination behavior, and API key handling.
limitations: Requires a connected Rube MCP server and an active Supabase connection.
Does not deploy edge functions or manage function source code.
Can expose or mutate live project data when used with admin credentials.
Relies on current Rube tool schemas, so users must search tools before workflows.

use_cases.title: Review database schema
use_cases.description: Developers can inspect tables, relationships, and generated types before writing queries.

use_cases.title: Check project operations
use_cases.description: Platform teams can review organizations, projects, service health, storage buckets, and edge functions.

use_cases.title: Run guarded SQL tasks
use_cases.description: Database owners can prepare read-only queries or approved data changes with schema checks first.

prompt_templates.title: List my projects
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Supabase automation skill to find my active Supabase projects through Rube MCP. Show names, refs, organizations, and health status if available.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a table schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the project named <project name>, list public tables, and summarize columns, relationships, indexes, and row counts for <table name>.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a safe query
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the schema for <table name>, then draft a read-only query plan for <business question>. Ask before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the target schema, identify required changes for <migration goal>, explain risks, and wait for approval before any write or DDL step.

output_examples.input: List projects and pick the one for production.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise project list with names, organization slugs, project references, regions, and notes on missing permissions.

output_examples.input: Inspect the users table before an update.
output_examples.output: You receive a schema summary with key columns, constraints, relationships, row count estimates, and a reminder to confirm writes.
The response summarizes selected services, current status, and any permission or scope errors.

best_practices: Search Rube tools first so parameter names and schemas match the current MCP server.
Use read-only mode for SELECT queries and require explicit approval for mutations.
Mask API keys and avoid storing Supabase secrets in chat, logs, or files.
anti_patterns: Running write SQL before inspecting schemas and confirming the target project.
Displaying full service-role keys or copying them into issue trackers.
Assuming organization IDs and slugs are interchangeable across Supabase tools.

faq.question: Does this skill require Supabase credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. A Rube MCP Supabase connection must be active before workflows can access projects.

faq.question: Can it run SQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide SQL execution through Supabase tools, including writes, so approval and read-only mode matter.

faq.question: Can it retrieve API keys?
faq.answer: Yes, it documents the API key tool. Users should mask keys and avoid exposing full values.

faq.question: Does it deploy edge functions?
faq.answer: No. It lists and retrieves edge function metadata, but it does not deploy functions.

faq.question: Why search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use current parameters.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: It can be used with care. Limit credentials, confirm destructive actions, and prefer read-only queries.
